exercises.en: Our daughter has big eyes like her mom.
exercises.why: Noun + 처럼 means 'like (noun)'.

exercises.ko: 제 친구는 한국 사람___ 한국어를 잘해요.
exercises.en: My friend speaks Korean well, like a Korean.
exercises.why: 처럼 attaches directly to the noun and works like an adverb.

exercises.en: I made kimbap the way my friend does.
exercises.why: To compare whole actions, use ~는 것처럼.

exercises.en: Minsu greeted me as if he were seeing me for the first time.
exercises.why: Modifier clause + 듯이 means 'as if'.

exercises.ko: 친구는 아침을 안 ___ 듯이 점심을 빨리 먹었어요.
exercises.en: My friend ate lunch quickly as if he hadn't eaten breakfast.
exercises.why: The past modifier ~은 before 듯이 means 'as if (he) had (not) done'.

exercises.ko: 그 사람은 밥 먹___ 거짓말을 해요.
exercises.en: That person lies as easily as eating (lit. like eating rice).
exercises.why: Stem + 듯이 builds a vivid simile.

exercises.en: Minsu seems very busy today.
exercises.why: Modifier + 듯하다 at the end of a sentence means 'it seems'.

exercises.en: That house is big, just like a hotel.
exercises.why: 마치 signals that a comparison with 처럼 is coming.

exercises.en: My younger sister sings like a singer.
He walked past as if he didn't know me.
It seems that the child is sleeping.
That person talks just like a teacher.

reading.ko: 제 친구 민수는 마치 선생님처럼 말해요. 민수는 상식이 아주 많아요. 어제 민수는 늦게까지 일했어요. 마감일이 오늘이에요. 오늘 아침에 민수는 잠을 못 잔 듯했어요. 민수는 아침을 안 먹은 듯이 빵을 빨리 먹었어요. 저도 민수처럼 열심히 일하고 싶어요.
reading.en: My friend Minsu talks just like a teacher. Minsu has a lot of common sense. Yesterday Minsu worked until late. The deadline is today. This morning Minsu seemed not to have slept. Minsu ate bread quickly as if he hadn't eaten breakfast. I want to work hard like Minsu too.

questions.a: 아침을 안 먹은 듯이 빨리 먹었어요.

exercises.en: This store is the only convenience store in our neighborhood.
exercises.why: 유일하다 is an adjective, so 유일한 describes the noun.

exercises.ko: 제가 ___ 할 수 있는 요리는 라면이에요.
exercises.en: The only dish I can make is ramen.
exercises.why: Before a verb you need the adverb form 유일하게.

exercises.en: The only animal I like at the zoo is the giraffe.
exercises.why: Before a noun use 유일한: ~는 유일한 (noun).

exercises.ko: 그 사람은 우리 회사에서 ___ 키가 큰 사람이에요.
exercises.en: He is the only tall person at our company.
exercises.why: 키가 큰 already describes the noun, so use the adverb 유일하게.

exercises.en: I am this restaurant's only regular customer.
exercises.why: 유일한 goes directly before the noun 단골.

exercises.ko: 제 친구 중에서 민수가 ___ 운전할 수 있어요.
exercises.en: Among my friends, Minsu is the only one who can drive.
exercises.why: 유일하게 is the adverb that goes before the verb.

exercises.en: These gloves are my only gloves.
exercises.why: Use 유일한 to describe a noun.

exercises.ko: 저는 우리 가족 중에서 ___ 고양이를 싫어해요.
exercises.en: I am the only one in my family who dislikes cats.
exercises.why: 유일하게 modifies the verb 싫어하다.

exercises.en: This is the only bag I have.
The only animal I dislike is the shark.
That person is the only person who helped me.
exercises.ko: 그 사람은 저를 도와준 유일한 사람이에요.

exercises.en: Minsu is the only person in our class who has a car.
exercises.ko: 민수는 우리 반에서 유일하게 차가 있는 사람이에요.

reading.ko: 저는 주말에 동물원에 갔어요. 동물원에는 사자, 기린, 코끼리, 독수리가 있었어요. 하지만 토끼는 없었어요. 제가 유일하게 좋아하는 동물은 토끼예요. 그래서 조금 슬펐어요. 동물원 앞에 작은 식당이 하나 있었어요. 그 식당은 동물원 근처의 유일한 식당이었어요.
reading.en: I went to the zoo on the weekend. At the zoo there were lions, giraffes, elephants and eagles. But there were no rabbits. The only animal I like is the rabbit. So I was a little sad. There was one small restaurant in front of the zoo. That restaurant was the only restaurant near the zoo.

questions.q: 이 사람이 유일하게 좋아하는 동물은 뭐예요?
동물원 근처에 식당이 몇 개 있었어요?

exercises.en: I only have 500 won in my pocket.
exercises.why: 밖에 must be followed by a negative predicate such as 없다.

exercises.en: I can only swim a little.
exercises.why: 밖에 needs a negative, so use 못.

exercises.ko: 역에서 우리 집까지 오 분___ 안 걸려요.
exercises.en: It only takes five minutes from the station to our house.
exercises.why: Time + 밖에 안 걸리다 stresses how short the time is.

exercises.en: There was no bus, so I had no choice but to take a taxi.
exercises.why: The pattern is future modifier ~ㄹ + 수밖에 없다.

exercises.ko: 숙제가 너무 많아서 오늘 밤에 공부할 수___ 없어요.
exercises.en: I have so much homework that I have no choice but to study tonight.
exercises.why: ~ㄹ/을 수밖에 없다 means 'have no choice but to'.

exercises.ko: 그 영화가 너무 슬퍼서 ___ 수밖에 없었어요.
exercises.en: The movie was so sad I couldn't help crying.
exercises.why: 울다 ends in ㄹ, so its future modifier is just 울.

exercises.en: I only wrote my name on the answer sheet.
exercises.why: Noun + 밖에 + negative means 'nothing but (noun)'.

exercises.ko: 비가 너무 많이 와서 집에 있을 수밖에 ___.
exercises.en: It rained so much that I had no choice but to stay home.
exercises.why: 수밖에 is always followed by 없다.

exercises.en: I only have one umbrella.
It only takes twenty minutes to the beach.
I only slept three hours.
I had no choice but to wait.

reading.ko: 오늘 저는 친구와 해변에 가고 싶었어요. 하지만 지갑에 만 원밖에 없었어요. 기차표는 이만 원이었어요. 돈이 모자라서 버스를 탈 수밖에 없었어요. 버스는 세 시간이 걸렸어요. 해변에는 사람이 몇 명밖에 없었어요. 조용해서 아주 좋았어요.
reading.en: Today I wanted to go to the beach with a friend. But I only had 10,000 won in my wallet. The train ticket was 20,000 won. I didn't have enough money, so I had no choice but to take the bus. The bus took three hours. There were only a few people at the beach. It was quiet, so it was very nice.

questions.a: 돈이 모자라서 버스를 탈 수밖에 없었어요.

exercises.en: I went to the market and bought fruit.
exercises.why: ~아/어서 links going somewhere with what you did there.

exercises.en: I walk to work every day.
exercises.why: 걷다 is ㄷ irregular, and ~어서 here shows the method.

exercises.en: I wrote a letter and sent it to my friend.
exercises.why: 쓰다 drops ㅡ: 쓰 + 어서 = 써서, and tense goes only on the last verb.

exercises.en: The puppy runs around inside the house.
exercises.why: 뛰다 + 어 + 다니다 forms the compound verb 뛰어다니다.

exercises.en: I put the bag on top of the chair.
exercises.why: 올리다 + 어 contracts to 올려, then joins 놓다.

exercises.en: I found out about it through the news.
exercises.why: Noun을/를 통해서 means 'through (noun)'.

exercises.ko: 저는 언니___ 통해서 남자 친구를 만났어요.
exercises.en: I met my boyfriend through my older sister.
exercises.why: 통하다 takes 을/를, and 언니 ends in a vowel.

exercises.en: I was late, so I hurriedly took a taxi.
exercises.why: 서두르다 is 르 irregular: 서둘러.

exercises.en: My puppy came running to me.
I went to the library and studied.
I learned Korean through movies.
Please let me know your phone number.

reading.ko: 오늘은 스승의 날이에요. 저는 아침에 늦게 일어나서 서둘러 집을 나갔어요. 학교까지 뛰어서 갔어요. 학교에 도착해서 선생님께 꽃을 드렸어요. 선생님께서 웃으시면서 고맙다고 말씀하셨어요. 저는 친구를 통해서 선생님이 꽃을 좋아하신다고 들었어요.
reading.en: Today is Teachers' Day. I got up late in the morning and hurried out of the house. I ran to school. When I arrived at school, I gave my teacher flowers. My teacher smiled and said thank you. I had heard through a friend that my teacher likes flowers.

questions.q: 누구를 통해서 선생님이 꽃을 좋아하신다고 들었어요?

exercises.ko: 이 여행 비용에는 비행기 표가 ___ 있어요.
exercises.en: The plane ticket is included in the cost of this trip.
exercises.why: The passive 포함되다 + ~어 있다 means 'is included'.

exercises.ko: 저___ 포함해서 일곱 명이 파티에 왔어요.
exercises.en: Seven people came to the party, including me.
exercises.why: 포함하다 takes an object, and 저 ends in a vowel.

exercises.en: I exercise every day except Saturday.
exercises.why: Use 제외하고 to split the sentence; 제외하다 doesn't take ~아/어서.

exercises.en: All the students except Minsu did their homework.
exercises.why: 제외한 + noun describes the noun that follows.

exercises.en: Please leave out the onion.
exercises.why: 빼다 + 아/어 주세요 becomes 빼 주세요.

exercises.en: Everyone saw the movie except me.
exercises.why: In speech, noun + 빼고 means 'except (noun)'.

exercises.ko: 저는 영어 ___ 일본어도 할 수 있어요.
exercises.en: Besides English, I can also speak Japanese.
exercises.why: Noun + 외에 means 'besides (noun)'.

exercises.en: How much is it if you include tax?
exercises.why: 포함하다 + ~면 means 'if you include'.

exercises.en: Is a drink included in this price?
Everyone came except my younger brother.
Please leave out the onion.
Besides dogs, I also like cats.

reading.ko: 저는 다음 달에 새 집으로 이사해요. 월세는 한 달에 오십만 원이에요. 월세에 가스비가 포함되어 있어요. 하지만 인터넷 비용은 포함되어 있지 않아요. 그 외에 다른 비용은 없어요. 일요일을 제외하고 매일 집을 볼 수 있어요. 저를 포함해서 세 명이 같이 집을 보러 갈 거예요.
reading.en: I'm moving to a new home next month. The rent is 500,000 won a month. The gas bill is included in the rent. But the internet fee is not included. Besides that, there are no other fees. You can see the house every day except Sunday. Three people, including me, will go to see the house together.

questions.q: 몇 명이 집을 보러 갈 거예요?

exercises.en: Minsu is as tall as his older brother.
exercises.why: Noun + 만큼 compares degree: 'as … as (noun)'.

exercises.en: Take as many as you want.
exercises.why: A modifier clause + 만큼 means 'as much as'.

exercises.en: The kimchi was so spicy that tears came out.
exercises.why: Exaggerated extent uses the future modifier: ~ㄹ 정도로.

exercises.ko: 서울에서 부산까지 기차로 세 시간 ___ 걸려요.
exercises.en: It takes about three hours by train from Seoul to Busan.
exercises.why: After a number, 정도 means 'about'.

exercises.en: How much Japanese do you know?
exercises.why: 어느 정도 asks 'to what extent'.

exercises.en: I got a good score in proportion to how much I studied.
exercises.why: Past modifier + 만큼 means 'to the extent that I did'.

exercises.en: I like exercising as much as singing.
exercises.why: ~는 것만큼 compares two actions by degree.

exercises.en: How much water shall I give you?
exercises.why: 얼마만큼 asks 'how much'.

exercises.en: Minsu is as tall as his dad.
It takes about thirty minutes to school.
I was so hungry I could die.
Buy as many as you need.

reading.ko: 어제 저는 친구들과 한국 식당에 갔어요. 열 명 정도 왔어요. 반찬이 정말 많았어요. 우리는 배가 터질 만큼 먹었어요. 김치는 눈물이 날 정도로 매웠어요. 제 친구 민수는 저만큼 매운 음식을 좋아해요. 그래서 우리 둘은 김치를 많이 먹었어요.
reading.en: Yesterday I went to a Korean restaurant with friends. About ten people came. There were really a lot of side dishes. We ate so much our stomachs could burst. The kimchi was so spicy it brought tears. My friend Minsu likes spicy food as much as I do. So the two of us ate a lot of kimchi.

exercises.en: I went to the airport instead of my dad.
exercises.why: Noun + 대신에 means 'instead of (noun)'.

exercises.en: Instead of taking a taxi, I took the subway.
exercises.why: ~는 대신에 always uses the present ~는 form, even for the past.

exercises.ko: 주말에 집에서 ___ 대신에 친구를 만날 거예요.
exercises.en: This weekend, instead of resting at home, I'll meet a friend.
exercises.why: Even for the future, use ~는 before 대신에.

exercises.en: If it's this expensive, I'd rather eat at home.
exercises.why: 차라리 shows you'd prefer this option.

exercises.en: Rather than waiting a long time for the bus, I'd rather walk.
exercises.why: 차라리 marks the option the speaker prefers.

exercises.en: Not the red one; the blue one, please.
exercises.why: Noun + 말고 means 'not X, (but Y)'.

exercises.en: Shall we meet on Sunday instead of Saturday?
exercises.why: 말고 follows a noun directly to reject it.

exercises.en: I put in honey instead of sugar.
exercises.why: Noun + 대신(에): the 에 can be dropped.

exercises.en: I drank juice instead of coffee.
Instead of watching TV, I studied.
I'd rather stay home.
Not tea; water, please.

reading.ko: 지난 주말에 저는 친척 집에 가야 했어요. 그런데 비가 굉장히 많이 왔어요. 그래서 버스를 타는 대신에 택시를 탔어요. 택시는 너무 비쌌어요. 집사람은 "다음에는 차라리 기차를 타요."라고 했어요. 친척 집에서 우리는 밥 대신에 국수를 먹었어요. 자정 무렵에 집에 돌아왔어요.
reading.en: Last weekend I had to go to my relatives' house. But it rained a lot. So instead of taking the bus, I took a taxi. The taxi was too expensive. My wife said, "Next time, let's just take the train." At my relatives' house, we ate noodles instead of rice. We came back home around midnight.

questions.a: 비가 굉장히 많이 와서 택시를 탔어요.

exercises.en: It doesn't matter if the food is a little spicy.
exercises.why: 맵다 is ㅂ irregular, and the condition takes ~아/어도.

exercises.en: It's fine if you open the window.
exercises.why: ~어도 상관없다 means 'it doesn't matter if'.

exercises.en: It doesn't matter who comes.
exercises.why: With a question word, ~든지 goes before 상관없다.

exercises.en: It doesn't matter where we eat.
exercises.why: With a question word, use ~는지 before 상관없다.

exercises.ko: 가격___ 상관없이 제일 좋은 것을 사고 싶어요.
exercises.en: Regardless of price, I want to buy the best one.
exercises.why: 가격 ends in a consonant, so it takes 과 before 상관없이.

exercises.en: I take a walk every day regardless of the weather.
exercises.why: 날씨 ends in a vowel, so it takes 와.

exercises.ko: 통증___ 불구하고 그 선수는 경기에 나갔다.
exercises.en: Despite the pain, the player went into the game. (written)
exercises.why: A noun takes ~에도 before 불구하고.

exercises.en: Despite having a lot of money, he was not happy. (written)
exercises.why: An adjective becomes a noun with ~음 before 에도 불구하고.

exercises.en: It doesn't matter if it's small.
It doesn't matter when we go.
I drink coffee regardless of the time.
Despite the injury, he worked hard. (written)

reading.ko: 제 친구는 다음 달에 시골로 이사할 거예요. 시골 집은 아주 작아요. 하지만 친구는 집 크기와 상관없이 시골이 좋다고 해요. 짐이 많아서 저는 친구를 도와줄 거예요. 친구는 "주말에 와도 상관없어."라고 했어요. 저는 토요일에 갈 거예요.
reading.en: My friend is going to move to the countryside next month. The house in the countryside is very small. But my friend says that, regardless of the size of the house, the countryside is good. There is a lot of luggage, so I'm going to help my friend. My friend said, "It's fine if you come on the weekend." I'm going to go on Saturday.

questions.q: 이 사람은 언제 친구를 도와주러 갈 거예요?

exercises.ko: 저는 다른 사람의 말에 신경 ___ 써요.
exercises.en: I don't care what other people say.
exercises.why: 안 goes right before the verb 쓰다.

exercises.ko: 제 남편은 돈___ 신경을 안 써요.
exercises.en: My husband doesn't care about money.
exercises.why: The thing you (don't) care about takes ~에.

exercises.en: I don't pay attention to my health.
exercises.why: ~에 대해 신경 안 쓰다 means 'not care about'.

exercises.en: Don't mind what I said.
exercises.why: Negative commands use ~지 마세요.

exercises.ko: 사람들이 저를 어떻게 ___ 신경 안 써요.
exercises.en: I don't care what people think of me.
exercises.why: With a question word, use ~는지 before 신경 안 쓰다.

exercises.en: I don't care even if the food is cold.
exercises.why: ~아/어도 means 'even if'; 차갑다 is ㅂ irregular.

exercises.en: Please pay attention to the children.
exercises.why: 쓰다 drops ㅡ before 어: 써 주세요.

exercises.en: I've been really bothered by work lately.
exercises.why: With 신경이, use the passive 쓰이다: 쓰여요.

exercises.en: I don't care about the weather.
exercises.ko: 저는 날씨에 대해 신경 안 써요.

exercises.en: Don't worry about the price.
I don't care what you eat. (casual)
exercises.ko: 네가 뭘 먹는지 신경 안 써.

exercises.en: Please pay attention when you drive.
exercises.ko: 운전할 때 신경 좀 써 주세요.

reading.ko: 제 친구 지민은 다른 사람의 말에 신경을 안 써요. 지민은 옷에도 별로 신경 쓰지 않아요. 하지만 건강에는 신경을 많이 써요. 매일 아침에 운동하고 야채를 많이 먹어요. 저는 요즘 입시 때문에 신경이 많이 쓰여요. 지민은 "너무 신경 쓰지 마. 너는 잘할 거야."라고 했어요.
reading.en: My friend Jimin doesn't care what other people say. Jimin doesn't care much about clothes either. But she pays a lot of attention to her health. Every morning she exercises and eats a lot of vegetables. These days I'm really stressed about entrance exams. Jimin said, "Don't worry too much. You'll do well."

questions.q: 이 사람은 왜 신경이 많이 쓰여요?
